title: Activity
intro: Use Activity to check whether a recent payload arrived and what OpenLDR recorded afterward. A payload is one batch of data, such as one webhook request or one CLI ingestion batch.
Use your own recent payloads. No sample data is required. The pictures follow the fictional patient sent in the Workflows test installation. An empty installation can have no recent payloads.
You need View activity. This page reads recorded events. It does not change, retry or delete the underlying data. Audit records user and administrative changes.

tasks.title: Follow one payload
intro: Use this when a sender asks whether its data arrived. Keep its response identifier or sending time nearby.
steps: Enter its identifier in Search payloads.... Search also matches source, status or stage within the loaded list.
Match the source and start time. Read the current stage and status. This example reached Persisted and Complete.
Select the row to open Payload lifecycle.
Copy the payload identifier shown below the sheet title when reporting a problem.
Read the arrival timestamp, source detail and associated run identifier. Use the run identifier when checking Workflows history.
Read the recorded storage event and resource counts. The example stored one Patient. Other workflows can record different stages.
tasks.result: You can identify the payload and the stages actually recorded for it.

tasks.title: Fetch the latest recorded state
intro: Use Refresh after new data arrives. Close and reopen a lifecycle sheet to fetch its current details.
steps: Select Refresh. Reopen the payload row when you need refreshed lifecycle details.

tasks.title: Show complete payloads
intro: Use Status filters when reviewing one outcome. Filters apply to the loaded recent payloads.
steps: Open the column selector and choose Status. Keep Equals.
Open the value selector and choose Complete. Choose a different status when investigating that outcome.
Select Apply. The rule appears above the table.
tasks.result: The visible rows match the Status rule.

tasks.title: Put latest start times first
intro: Use a time sort when arrival order matters. It changes the loaded list only.
steps: Select Asc once to change it to Desc.
Select Apply. Latest start times appear first.

tasks.title: Choose visible columns
intro: Use this when the table is wider than the information you need.
steps: Use the column checkboxes to show or hide fields. Keep Payload visible so you can identify rows. Close the menu when finished.
Use the page size and navigation arrows below the table when the loaded list spans several pages.

tasks.title: Read a payload on a phone
intro: Search first to reduce a wide table. Scroll the table horizontally when you need columns farther right.
steps: Use the search field at the top of Activity.
Select its identifier in the row.
Scroll the sheet to read the recorded stages and resource counts.

end.title: Read stages and statuses
html:
StageMeaning
ReceivedAn ingestion batch or workflow recorded arrival.
ValidatedA workflow recorded a successful check.
PersistedA storage event recorded saved resources.
PushedA step recorded delivery to another system.

StatusMeaning
CompleteData reached storage without a recorded failed workflow run.
FailedA related workflow run or ingestion batch failed.
StuckThe recorded events do not establish completion or failure.
RunningAn import run or CLI batch is still active.
StoppedAn import run or CLI batch was stopped.
paragraphs: The stage bar highlights stages up to the latest recorded stage. Read the lifecycle itself to see which events actually exist. A missing Validated stage does not prove that every earlier check failed.
A recorded push does not prove the recipient accepted or read the data. Stuck is not proof that processing stopped. Check the workflow History and its node results.

end.title: Understand the history window
paragraphs: Activity loads up to 200 recent payloads. Search, filters, sorting and paging act on those loaded rows. They do not search the full database.

CLI batch history also has its own limit. For older ingestion batches, use openldr pipeline status. Read Start here for the installed launcher or the development form pnpm openldr pipeline status. Use your real installation folder, such as ~/Downloads/openldr_ce or C:\openldr_ce.

end.title: Optional fictional practice
paragraphs: You can follow any received payload without creating more data. For test practice, use the optional fictional Bundle in Workflows. Complete its webhook steps, then match the returned correlation identifier here. No sample is required in normal use.

end.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: The list is empty. Clear search and filters, then Refresh. Check sender responses and Workflows History before deciding nothing arrived. Older events can be outside the recent window.
A row is Failed. Open the workflow History and inspect the failing node. Activity has no retry action. Reconcile effects before following the workflow recovery procedure.

The sheet stays on Loading. Close it, Refresh, and reopen the row. If it persists, ask an administrator to check the API request and server logs. This sheet cannot distinguish every failed request from a slow one.
Refresh shows an error. Try once again. Report the exact error if it persists.

end.title: Related guides
paragraphs: Workflows explains runs and webhook receipts. Audit explains administrative change records.
